## Cleaning data

\

data : main dataframe\
parameter : IMPC parameter data frame\
procedure : IMPC procedure data frame\

***Steps*** ***for each dataset***

[**gene_symbol**]{.underline}

- Based on the Guidleines for Nomenclature of Genes in Mouse,(<https://www.informatics.jax.org/nomen/gene.shtml?utm_source=chatgpt.com#gnas>), a gene symbol begins with uppercase followed by all lowercase/numbers, with several exceptions :

  - it can start with sequence identifier ex : 0610009F21Rik,

  - it can with start lowercase letter if the gene is only identified by recessive mutant phenotype

  - possible uppercase after the initial letter in certain cases.

- Specific punctuations that are allowed are : hyphens and (). Hyphens are used to separate related sequence and pseudogene symbol from root

- Manually cleaning the data turns out to be impossible without reference data, resort to alternative cleaning : replacing all gene symbol value with reference from MGI website based on their gene accession id

[Importing reference for gene_symbols]{.underline}

```{r}
##Importing the official MGI gene list 
readLines("./References/MGI_genesymbol_ref.rpt", n = 2)
ref_genesymbol <- read.delim("./References/MGI_genesymbol_ref.rpt", header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)

#extracting only the column of gene accession id and gene symbol name 
ref_genesymbol <- ref_genesymbol %>% 
  select("MGI Accession ID", "Marker Symbol")

```

[Tried attempt for manual cleaning]{.underline}

```{r}
])

#genes like 1700029H14Rik are acceptable according to guideline

# hyphen as initial letter of gene symbol is not part of the guideline's exception so we exclude them

unique_symbols

  unique_symbols %in% ref_genesymbol$`Marker Symbol`
]
included_symbols

#removing all illegitimate hyphens

]) #none

comparison <- data %>%
  distinct(gene_symbol) %>%
  filter(!gene_symbol %in% ref_genesymbol$`Marker Symbol`)

###still hundreds of non-uniform forms of misspelling
### cleaning proof to be too tiresome, will resolve to replacing all gene symbols based on MGI Accesion id
}
```

Alternative cleaning :

- In the end, chosed to replace all values with reference data from website (MRK List2)\
  <https://www.informatics.jax.org/downloads/reports/index.html>

```{r}
#replace all genesymbol with reference Marker Symbol based on its corresponding MGI Accesion ID
data <- data %>%
  left_join(
    ref_genesymbol %>%
      select(`MGI Accession ID`, `Marker Symbol`),
    by = c("gene_accession_id" = "MGI Accession ID")) %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = coalesce(`Marker Symbol`, gene_symbol)) %>%
  select(-`Marker Symbol`)

#checking any unsuccessful replacement
sum(is.na(data$gene_symbol)) #0, all successful 
```

[**parameter_id**]{.underline}

- Standardized phenotyping parameters for IMPC IMPReSS database is IMPC_ECG_007_001 (<https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/impc-solr-api/overview-of-key-impc-concepts-and-tools/the-structure-of-impc-data-pipeline-procedure-parameter/>)
- Corrected injections of junk characters, and removal of multiple \_

```{r}
#checking missing IDs
sum(is.na(data$parameter_stable_id))

#removing unrelevant characters
data$parameter_stable_id <- str_remove_all(data$parameter_stable_id, "[-!@#$%^&*()+.]")

#checking remaining unexpected characters after removal
sum(!is.na(data$parameter_stable_id) &
      grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", data$parameter_stable_id)) #0

#make all upper case
data$parameter_stable_id <- toupper(data$parameter_stable_id)

#checking any remaining format error
unique(data$parameter_stable_id[
  !grepl("^[A-Z0-9]+_[A-Z0-9]+_[0-9]+_[0-9]+$", data$parameter_stable_id) &
    !is.na(data$parameter_stable_id)
])

#we have identified several problems : multiple_, and _ in wrong positions

#remove all _ 
x <- str_remove_all(data$parameter_stable_id, "_")

#put _ back in appropriate places
x <- str_replace(x, "^([A-Z]+)([A-Z]{3})(\\d{3})(\\d{3})$", "\\1_\\2_\\3_\\4")   # e.g. IMPC_CSD_039_001
x <- str_replace(x, "^([A-Z]+)(\\d{3})(\\d{3})(\\d{3})$",   "\\1_\\2_\\3_\\4")   # e.g. MGP_026_001_006
data$parameter_stable_id <- x

#checking any remaining format error again
unique(data$parameter_stable_id[
  !grepl("^[A-Z0-9]+_[A-Z0-9]+_[0-9]+_[0-9]+$", data$parameter_stable_id) &
    !is.na(data$parameter_stable_id)
]) #0
```

[1.1. Grouped parameter into 8 broad groups]{.underline}

The grouping is done by grouping procedure identifier (middle suffix) on IMPC standard pipeline nomenclature (ex : EYE in IMPC\_ EYE_001_001). See ref_parameter_group.csv on References folder for the complete list.

```{r}
#import reference csv
references <- read.csv("./References/ref_parameter_groups.csv")
colnames(references)

#extract middle suffix and create a new column
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(suffix = str_extract(parameter_stable_id, "(?<=_)[^_]+"))

#join to the reference by suffix and create a new column for suffix_desc
data <- data %>% 
  left_join(references %>% select(suffix, suffix_desc), by = c("suffix"))

data <-  data %>% 
  relocate(suffix, suffix_desc, .after= parameter_stable_id)
  
# Grouping by suffix
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      
      # 1. Weight and body composition
      suffix %in% c("OWT", "HWT", "020", "005", "DXA", "BWT") ~
        "Weight and body composition",
      
      # 2. Brain, behaviour and neurological function
      suffix %in% c(
        "SLW", "LDT", "OFD", "007", "FEA", "HBD",
        "TLS", "ROT", "ACS", "011", "ABR", "ECT",
        "TFL", "012", "008", "CSD", "GRS", "009",
        "FOR", "YMZ"
      ) ~ "Brain, behaviour and neurological function",
      
      # 3. Imaging and morphology
      suffix %in% c(
        "EYE", "014", "013", "XRY", "006", "XMV",
        "GEL", "GEM", "GEO", "GEP", "GPL", "GPM",
        "GPO", "GPP", "001", "026", "ERG",
        "EMA", "MAA", "EML", "EOL", "EMO"
      ) ~ "Imaging and morphology",
      
      # 4. Cardiovascular and respiratory function
      suffix %in% c("ECH", "ECG", "LFO", "CHL") ~
        "Cardiovascular and respiratory function",
      
      # 5. Blood, clinical chemistry and metabolism
      suffix %in% c(
        "CBC", "025", "015", "HEM", "016", "PLC",
        "INS", "IPG", "004", "003", "CAL", "021", "URI"
      ) ~ "Blood, clinical chemistry and metabolism",
      
      # 6. Immune system and immunophenotyping
      suffix %in% c(
        "IMM", "MLN", "PBI", "BMI", "EEI",
        "019", "ANA", "018", "023"
      ) ~ "Immune system and immunophenotyping",
      
      # 7. Histopathology and Tissue Analysis
      suffix %in% c("HIS", "PAT", "ALZ", "HOU", "WEL", "BLK") ~
        "Histopathology and Tissue Analysis",
      
      # 8. Reproductive and developmental biology
      suffix %in% c(
        "FER", "VIA", "EVL", "EVM", "EVO", "EVP",
        "EXD", "ELZ"
      ) ~ "Reproductive and developmental biology",
      
      # Keep unmatched and missing suffixes as NA
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  relocate(group, .after = suffix_desc)

#Check grouping
data %>%
  count(group, sort = TRUE) 
  
#check any ungrouped data
data %>%
  filter(is.na(group)) %>%
  distinct(suffix, suffix_desc)
```

**allele_symbol**

- Tried replacing all values with reference from MGI website : [https://www.informatics.jax.org/downloads/reports/MGI_PhenotypicAllele.rp](https://www.informatics.jax.org/downloads/reports/MGI_PhenotypicAllele.rpt){.uri}t but it does not work because gene_accession_id correspond to multiple allele_symbol and we cannot make sure which ones are used. The ideal solution is to ask the researcher whether they have the specific allele_id rather than gene_id.

```{r}
#keep only MGI_id and reference allele name
```


Attempt manual cleaning according to the convention of allele names\
Will not be 100% accurate to the reference, but we figured at least its close enough to enable search later on and alleles_symbol are not used in further downstream analyses

```{r}
#Allele symbols allowed ()*/<> but not other junk characters
#remove any inappropiate junk symbols
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    allele_symbol = str_remove_all(
      allele_symbol,
      "[^A-Za-z0-9()*/<>]"
    ))

#Remove any inappropiate junk characters before <>, junk characters that are allowed in gene symbol is only - and (), but in our previous analysis when cleaning gene_symbol manually none of the () found are appropiate, so we will exclude them 
data <- data %>%
  mutate(allele_symbol = str_replace(allele_symbol,"^[^<]*",
      function(x) str_remove_all(x, "[^A-Za-z0-9-]")
    ))

#check if there are still any gene symbol that dont match 
sum(
  str_extract(data$allele_symbol, "^[^<]+") != data$gene_symbol,
  na.rm = TRUE) #456 does not match 

#View which ones are not matching
data %>%
  filter(str_extract(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+") != gene_symbol) %>%
  select(gene_symbol, allele_symbol) 

##some are case sensitive, some have minor one or two letters deletion/insertion
#and some have different gene name 

#addressing gene name that have exact same letter but different case 
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    allele_prefix = str_extract(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+"),
    allele_symbol = if_else(
      !is.na(allele_prefix) &
        !is.na(gene_symbol) &
        str_to_lower(allele_prefix) == str_to_lower(gene_symbol),
      str_replace(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+", gene_symbol),
      allele_symbol)) %>%
  select(-allele_prefix)

#checking again, if case difference cases have been fixed
#save it into variable called allele_checking
allele_checking <- data %>%
  filter(str_extract(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+") != gene_symbol) %>%
  select(gene_symbol, allele_symbol)

#distinguishing minor one/two letter difference vs totally different gene using Levenshtein distance
allele_checking <- allele_checking %>%
  mutate(allele_prefix = str_extract(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+"),
    distance = stringdist(
      str_to_lower(allele_prefix),
      str_to_lower(gene_symbol),
      method = "lv")) %>%
  select(gene_symbol, allele_symbol, allele_prefix, distance)

#fixing only levenshtein distance = 1, which signify only minor one letter differences
data <- data %>%
  mutate(allele_prefix = str_extract(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+"),
    distance = stringdist(
      str_to_lower(allele_prefix),
      str_to_lower(gene_symbol),
      method = "lv"),
    allele_symbol = if_else(
      !is.na(distance) & distance == 1,
      str_replace(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+", gene_symbol),
      allele_symbol)) %>%
  select(-allele_prefix, -distance)

#selecting levenshtein distacne >1, which signify completely different gene name
#we then check their MGI id with the reference to see the correct values
allele_checking <- data %>%
  mutate(
    allele_prefix = str_extract(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+"),
    distance = stringdist(
      str_to_lower(allele_prefix),
      str_to_lower(gene_symbol),
      method = "lv")) %>%
  filter(distance > 1) %>%
  select(gene_accession_id, gene_symbol, allele_symbol, allele_prefix, distance)


#match the eronous MGI_id with the allele name from the reference 
allele_ref_checking <- allele_ref %>%
  filter(MGI_id %in% allele_checking$gene_accession_id) %>%
  select(MGI_id, allele)


joinedcheck <- allele_checking %>%
  left_join(
    allele_ref_checking %>%
      select(MGI_id, allele),
    by = c("gene_accession_id" = "MGI_id"))

#as expected, our data allele symbol input have different gene name. Matching via gene_accession_id (gene symbol) alone is not enough because one gene can have many different allele symbols. Without allele_symbol_id we cannot infer which one is the correct one, therefore we decided to make these value NA. We will store these erronous gene-accesion_id (allele_checking dataframe) to give to the researcher incase they will do crosscheck on their analysis data.  

#change all completely different gene name into NA
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    allele_prefix = str_extract(allele_symbol, "^[^<]+"),
    distance = stringdist(
      str_to_lower(allele_prefix),
      str_to_lower(gene_symbol),
      method = "lv"
      ),
    allele_symbol = if_else(
      !is.na(distance) & distance > 1,
      NA,
      allele_symbol
    )) %>%
  select(-allele_prefix, -distance)

write.csv(allele_checking, "./Cleaned_data/mismatched_allelesymbols.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

So far, these manual cleaning has ensure that gene_symbol part of allele_symbol matches the reference gene_accession_id.

Note that this manual method of cleaning have one caveat. This method assumes that both the gene_symbol\<allele designation\> are approximately acccurate. This method cannot take into account if the allele designation is completelely different designation for that aprticular gene symbol. Should there be more time and computing resource, a more advanced algorithm of searching the nearest string match to the reference, followed by manual crosscheck, would be the ideal solution to this problem.

## Data Cleaning - Parameter

- parameters grouped from IMPC website for the testing they are related to.

  - ref_paramater_groups.csv needed is in repo, contains all groups for reference. Some parameters are in twice but with different impcParameterOrigId so these have been retained for now.

- duplicates from impcParameterOrigid removed.

```{r}
# code to group the parameters based on the IMPC protocols
references <- read.csv("./References/ref_parameter_groups.csv", header = TRUE)

precleaned_parameter$suffix <- sub("^[^_]*_([^_]*)_.*$", "\\1",
                                     precleaned_parameter$parameterId)

precleaned_parameter <- precleaned_parameter %>%
  left_join(
    references %>% select(suffix, suffix_desc),
    by = "suffix")

# handling repeats
precleaned_parameter %>%
  filter(duplicated(impcParameterOrigId))
# repeat of GRS parameters found
precleaned_parameter %>%
  filter(duplicated(impcParameterOrigId))
# removing repeats
precleaned_parameter <- precleaned_parameter %>%
  distinct(impcParameterOrigId, .keep_all = TRUE)

parameter <- precleaned_parameter

parameter <- parameter %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      
      # 1. Weight and body composition
      suffix %in% c("OWT", "HWT", "020", "005", "DXA", "BWT") ~
        "Weight and body composition",
      
      # 2. Brain, behaviour and neurological function
      suffix %in% c(
        "SLW", "LDT", "OFD", "007", "FEA", "HBD",
        "TLS", "ROT", "ACS", "011", "ABR", "ECT",
        "TFL", "012", "008", "CSD", "GRS", "009",
        "FOR", "YMZ"
      ) ~ "Brain, behaviour and neurological function",
      
      # 3. Imaging and morphology
      suffix %in% c(
        "EYE", "014", "013", "XRY", "006", "XMV",
        "GEL", "GEM", "GEO", "GEP", "GPL", "GPM",
        "GPO", "GPP", "001", "026", "ERG",
        "EMA", "MAA", "EML", "EOL", "EMO"
      ) ~ "Imaging and morphology",
      
      # 4. Cardiovascular and respiratory function
      suffix %in% c("ECH", "ECG", "LFO", "CHL") ~
        "Cardiovascular and respiratory function",
      
      # 5. Blood, clinical chemistry and metabolism
      suffix %in% c(
        "CBC", "025", "015", "HEM", "016", "PLC",
        "INS", "IPG", "004", "003", "CAL", "021", "URI"
      ) ~ "Blood, clinical chemistry and metabolism",
      
      # 6. Immune system and immunophenotyping
      suffix %in% c(
        "IMM", "MLN", "PBI", "BMI", "EEI",
        "019", "ANA", "018", "023"

  ) %>%
  relocate(group, .after = suffix_desc)

#check any unassigned variable
parameter %>%
  filter(is.na(suffix_desc)) %>%
  distinct(suffix, suffix_desc, group)


#checking if there is any duplicated IMPC orig id left 
sum(duplicated(parameter$impcParameterOrigId))

#Verifying all ids are compliant
precleaned_parameter %>%
  filter(!grepl("^IMPC_.{3}_.{3}_.{3}$", parameterId))


```

## Data Cleaning - Procedure

- No cleaning needed to be done

```{r}
#Checking if there are duplication caused by  msisspeling or different case within the same group (ex histopathOlogy vs Histopathology)
unique(procedure$proc_name) #all unique
unique(procedure$proc_desc) #all unique

unique(procedure$isMandatory) #no other values except TRUE or FALSE

#checking if there are only numbers in paramater orig id
all(grepl("[0-9]", procedure$impcParameterOrigId)) #TRUE
#checking id there are duplicates in parameter orig id
sum(duplicated(procedure$impcParameterOrigId)) #0

```

## Data Cleaning - Disease

- No cleaning needed to be done

```{r}
#Strings variables such as human_name, and do_term are briefly screened for any possible error 
unique(disease$human_name)
unique(disease$do_term)
#No error detected


#checking if human_symbol is uppercased and have no special character
all(grepl("^[A-Z0-9]+$", disease$human_symbol), na.rm = TRUE) #FALSE
#there are some that has, checking 
unique(disease$human_symbol[grepl("[a-z]", disease$human_symbol)])
unique(disease$human_symbol[grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9]", disease$human_symbol)])
# all special characters and lowercase follows convention, no cleaning needed

#checking if mouse_symbol first letter is uppercased and have no special characters
all(grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", disease$mouse_symbol), na.rm = TRUE) #FALSE
#there are some that had, checking
unique(disease$mouse_symbol[!grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", disease$mouse_symbol)])
#all special characters and lowercase follows convention, no cleaning needed

#Checking if id columns follow their conventions
all(grepl("^HGNC:.*[0-9]+$", disease$hgnc_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE
all(grepl("^DOID:.*[0-9]+$", disease$do_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE
all(grepl("^MGI:.*[0-9]+$", disease$mgi_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE


```

## Data Cleaning - Bespoke

- change the column date into a Date format

```{r}
#Checking if there are special characters in DB obj id 
all(grepl("[a-zA-Z0-9]", bespoke$DB_obj_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE

#Checking if there are special characters, and all gene start with uppercase
all(grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", bespoke$DB_obj_symbol), na.rm = TRUE) #FALSE
#there are some that had, checking
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_symbol[!grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", bespoke$DB_obj_symbol)])
#all special characters follow convention, no cleaning needed

#checking the notation
all(grepl("^GO:[0-9]", bespoke$GO_id), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE
all(grepl("^GO_REF:[0-9]", bespoke$DB_reference), na.rm = TRUE) #TRUE

#checking if there are special characters and all starts with uppercase
all(grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-z0-9]", bespoke$DB_obj_synonym), na.rm = TRUE)
#there are some that has, checking 
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_synonym[!grepl("^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$", bespoke$DB_obj_synonym)])
# all special characters follow convention, no cleaning needed

unique(bespoke$date) #all 20261009
#change into date
bespoke$date <- as.Date(
  format(bespoke$date, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
  format = "%Y%m%d"
)

unique(bespoke$DB) #all 1 value
unique(bespoke$Relation) #no other value expcept located_in, enables, involved_in, and part_of
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_type) #all protein
unique(bespoke$taxon) #all taxon: 10090
unique(bespoke$evidence_code) #all value is IEA
unique(bespoke$with_from) #no misspelling
unique(bespoke$aspect) #no other calues than C,F and P
unique(bespoke$DB_obj_name) #brief scanning shows no error
unique(bespoke$assigned_by) #no other value than UniProt and GOC
unique(bespoke$annotation_exp) #all NAs
unique(bespoke$Gene_product_formid) #all NAs
```

### 5. Save cleaned files

```{r}
#rearrange column order
data <- data %>% 
  relocate(analysis_id, .after = file) %>% 
  relocate(p_value, .after = mouse_life_stage) 

#saving env as R.data
save(data, parameter, procedure, disease, bespoke, file = "./Cleaned_data/Cleaned_data.Rdata")

#saving as csv
write.csv(data, "./Cleaned_data/Cleaned_analysis.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(parameter, "./Cleaned_data/Cleaned_parameter.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(procedure, "./Cleaned_data/Cleaned_procedure.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(disease, "./Cleaned_data/Cleaned_disease.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(bespoke, "./Cleaned_data/Cleaned_bespoke.csv", row.names= FALSE)

View(data)
View(parameter)
View(procedure)
View(disease)
View(bespoke)
```
